C-EXT-DELIVERY-HONESTY.Summary: Make M-045's delivery and publication honest at their three failure surfaces: a doc_open whose frontend emission fails refuses the open instead of answering accepted:true over an undelivered stream; the live-endpoint publication that tells external consumers where the live server listens gains a bounded, surfaced retry for transient write failures with a final state that is textually distinct from "the server did not start"; and the outbound invoke error path bounds and sanitizes the extension-controlled response body so no unbounded, control-bearing foreign material reaches the journal or the renderer.
C-EXT-DELIVERY-HONESTY.Problem: Verified against the current worktree (branch spec/ext-delivery-honesty, base 1dbe9bb9, all landed waves merged); wave-2 scout findings 18, 20 and 10 — bundle B4, the last unlanded bundle of the four triaged from the 2026-11-22 scout. One cause: the delivery/publication layer behaves as if success were the only observable outcome, and the one place foreign-controlled material enters Mark's surfaces it passes unfiltered. (1) STREAM-INVISIBLE: handle_doc_open (live_server.rs:1398) authenticates under the stream fence (1403), holds stream_gate (1409), passes the decide_open conflict/resync classification (1421-1453) and the C-STREAM-BUDGET caps (1475-1512), assigns the monotonic session_epoch (1515), stores the session (1535), emits doc_open (1540-1550) — and on emit failure only logs BLOCK_DOC_OPEN_EMIT_FAILED (1547-1549) before answering 200 DocOpenResponse {accepted: true, revision: 1} (1552-1563). The extension believes a live stream exists while nothing reached the renderer; every later patch is accepted and answered success by the server while the frontend, holding no live document, drops it — PATCH_LIVE_DOCUMENT refuses without an active binding (store/editor.js:1684-1689) and LiveViewer drops patches while not live (liveViewer/index.vue:65, the fail-closed isLive gate). The store's own null paths are correct refusals, not bugs: OPEN_LIVE_DOCUMENT returns null when the document window is closing, on a stale or malformed epoch and when the tab factory fails (store/editor.js:1656-1666) — the C-SEC-STREAM-TABS fail-closed contract working as designed. The dishonesty is the server's accepted:true over an undelivered open; there is no ack channel and no retry (treatment is re-open, which lies again the same way). (2) SERVER-RESTART: the live server and its discovery endpoint are published exactly once in the setup spawn of the in-source M-045 B5a block (main.rs:817-852): start_live_server Ok writes live-endpoint.json once (838-843); a write failure logs BLOCK_ENDPOINT_WRITE_FAILED (840-843) and a start failure logs BLOCK_START_FAILED (845-849) — log-only one-shots. No retry, no second publication attempt, no UI surface: a transient endpoint write failure leaves an external consumer without live-endpoint.json for the whole process lifetime, indistinguishable in its effect from a server that never started, and the only remedy is restarting the application. (3) ERRBODY-UNFILTERED: the outbound invoke reads the extension-controlled error body raw (let body_text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default(), invoke.rs:219) and embeds it verbatim into InvokeError.message (format!("HTTP {status}: {body_text}"), 224-227); Display (71-75) carries that message into the journal through BLOCK_INVOKE_FAILED reason={e} (mod.rs:297-299), and the same unfiltered text is returned to the renderer (format!("{e}"), mod.rs:300). The body is unbounded, may carry any control characters the extension chooses, and reaches both Mark's log and its renderer on every non-2xx extension answer.
C-EXT-DELIVERY-HONESTY.Relationship: Lineage, all landed. C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH owns the stream fence this handler still runs — authenticate_stream, stream_gate ordering, the monotonic session_epoch and ordered event identity are untouched. C-SEC-STREAM-TABS owns the renderer/store half of delivery: OPEN_LIVE_DOCUMENT's null-on-invalid contract, PATCH_LIVE_DOCUMENT's binding gate and LiveViewer's fail-closed isLive are preserved byte-for-byte in meaning — this change makes the server stop creating the false-accepted state those fences correctly contain, so the frontend needs no change ("the server does not lie" is sufficient). C-STREAM-BUDGET owns /stream/* refusal semantics: the 413 section/byte refusals (live_server.rs:1475-1512) and the 429 rate refusal keep their statuses, bodies, budgets and zero-mutation meaning; the emit-failure refusal is a new, distinct branch additive to the response vocabulary and charges no budget. C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF (#321) owns the invoke client's reliability policy — its idempotency key, Retry-After handling and single-retry attempt budget (invoke.rs:42-50, 92-100, 162-246) are untouched; this change touches only what the error message carries and what the renderer mapping exposes. C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE (#326) owns the disable fences and the enable/revoke-pending lifecycle — untouched. C-EXT-GALLERY-STATE (B3: scout keys 4, 13-16) has not landed on this base and remains a neighboring bundle, explicitly out of scope here. This bundle closes the delivery/publication half of the wave-2 acceptance criterion — on refusal the client sees the refusal — for the stream and endpoint paths: an undeliverable open refuses, an unpublished address becomes a bounded-retried, distinctly named state, and foreign error material is bounded, control-safe and labeled.

Goals.Goal: Honest open (STREAM-VISIBILITY): a doc_open whose frontend emission fails refuses the open. The handler rolls the just-stored session back to the pre-open guard value — None on a fresh open, the replaced session on a same-session resync — so no ghost session survives; the consumed epoch is retired (the counter stays monotonic and the value is never reused); the refusal is a non-2xx answer in the file's plain {"error": ...} voice with a distinct logged state beside the existing BLOCK_DOC_OPEN_EMIT_FAILED. The success path is unchanged: an emission that succeeds keeps the exact 200 DocOpenResponse contract and the ordered-identity event. A refused open accepts no patches (no session exists), and a client that re-opens after a refusal gets a fresh, strictly higher epoch — the existing resync path stays the recovery route, now backed by an honest gate.

Bounded, surfaced endpoint publication (ENDPOINT-PUBLICATION): the live-endpoint.json publication moves into a bounded retry helper beside the endpoint file I/O (live_endpoint.rs) with named attempt-count and inter-attempt pause constants and an injected writer so tests are deterministic; main.rs's setup spawn calls it in place of the single write_endpoint call. Every retried attempt is a distinct log marker; exhausting the budget ends in a distinct final state whose meaning is "the live server is running on port P but its address is unpublished after N attempts" — textually and semantically distinct from BLOCK_START_FAILED's "no server". A first-attempt success behaves exactly as today (one write, the existing BLOCK_WRITE_OK log).

Bounded, sanitized invoke errors (ERRBODY): every InvokeError.message is bounded under a named constant, and the extension-controlled BadStatus body is sanitized before entering it — control characters neutralized, content over the bound replaced by an explicit truncation marker carrying the original size — so the journal line (Display through BLOCK_INVOKE_FAILED) carries bounded, control-safe, labeled material only. The renderer-facing error returned by mt_ext_invoke is composed without the extension response body: the failure class, the HTTP status where one exists, and a body-withheld note. The invoke request path, retry policy, idempotency key and success path are unchanged.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope, enumerated by reading the current tree:

Read-only anchors: src/renderer/src/store/editor.js — the START_BLOCK_LIVE_DOCUMENT_OWNERSHIP block (1655-1682) keeps its null-on-invalid semantics exactly; src/renderer/src/components/liveViewer/index.vue — the fail-closed isLive gate (58-67) stays; editor.vue, textOps.js and every other renderer file are outside the scope; registry.rs, auth.rs, discovery.rs, text_ops.rs, manifest.rs and m001_validate.rs are untouched; main.rs is touched only inside the in-source M-045 B5a setup block (817-852), and the LiveServerState literal (822-828) stays textually unchanged — the emit-failure injection seam lives inside m045_ext (live_bridge.rs/live_server.rs), not in the shared state.

Wire discipline: request shapes are unchanged everywhere; /stream/open's success response keeps the DocOpenResponse fields (live_server.rs:323-326) with their names and meaning; the new emit-failure refusal is a non-2xx plain error body following the handler's existing refusal vocabulary (401/409/413 precedents); the C-STREAM-BUDGET 413/429 responses keep their exact statuses, bodies and zero-mutation semantics, and the refusal branch runs after the budget checks so it can neither relax nor re-order them. doc_patch, doc_close and heartbeat-timeout close keep today's log-only emit-failure behavior — the open is the delivery gate (see NonGoals).

Frontend preserved: the C-SEC-STREAM-TABS store contract — null on a closing window, on a stale or malformed epoch and on tab-factory failure, the epoch/binding-gated patch, the fail-closed live indicator — is unchanged and stays meaningful; this change removes the server-side lie that made those fences contain a phantom stream, and adds no renderer work.

Bounded and named: the endpoint publication attempt count and inter-attempt pause are named constants (the total retry window stays of the order of the current single write — no unbounded loop, no background republication); the invoke message bound is a named constant of the order of a few hundred characters; the truncation marker states the withheld original size; no new unbounded memory, channel, queue or timer anywhere.

Security hygiene unchanged: sanitization only removes and bounds material in logs and UI, never adds; no document content, token or secret material enters any new marker or error body; the loopback-only binding, Bearer model, capability/grant gates and the stream fence ordering (authenticate_stream, stream_gate, session lock) are untouched; control-character neutralization prevents log-injection through foreign bodies.

No new user-facing UI strings: every new surface is a log marker or a machine-facing error body in the existing English technical voice; the repository ten-locale canon (C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 precedent) is not triggered and no static/locales file is in the write scope (the C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF precedent for UI-free changes).

Predecessor suites keep meaning with zero moved pins: the C-STREAM-BUDGET suites, the stream security suite (stream_events_keep_ordered_identity_and_disable_only_closes_its_owner and neighbors), the #321 invoke suites (invoke_carries_stable_idempotency_key_across_retries, invoke_retries_429_once_honoring_retry_after, invoke_retry_after_over_ceiling_waits_no_longer_than_ceiling, invoke_honest_loopback_ok, invoke_redirect_response_not_followed, probe_health_honest_loopback_ok), the #326 trust suites and the live-store/liveViewer vitest suites pass with unchanged assertions. No existing test exercises an emit failure, an endpoint write failure or a non-2xx body's content, so this change moves no existing pin; every new pin is a new failing-first test.

Repository artifacts stay English and the GRACE surface is synchronized (module contracts and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries of main.rs, live_server.rs, live_bridge.rs, live_endpoint.rs, invoke.rs, mod.rs, tests.rs; module maps; graph; verification); no version change, release, publication or deploy is authorized by this specification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No edit-pipeline work (scout keys 1, 2, 3, 11, 17, 19 — bundle B1, C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF #321, landed): no doc_open ack channel or delivery-retry protocol — the honest refusal replaces it; no change to invoke idempotency, Retry-After handling or the attempt budget; no /ext/apply, /ext/text-insert or text_ops work.
No trust-lifecycle work (scout keys 5, 7, 8, 12 — bundle B2, C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE #326, landed): no disable, revoke, enable-gate or pairing work.
No gallery-state work (scout keys 4, 13, 14, 15, 16 — bundle B3, neighboring bundle, not landed): no registry, discovery, toggle or list-freshness work.

No mid-stream emit-failure redesign: doc_patch, doc_close and the heartbeat-timeout close keep today's log-only emit-failure behavior (live_server.rs:1789-1801, 1871-1882, 2574-2586); no event replay, no delivery queue, no ack channel, no frontend re-request. The open-time refusal plus the existing same-session resync are the recovery route — a client whose delivery is down now learns it at open instead of streaming into a void.

No renderer work and no new UI surface: store/editor.js, liveViewer/index.vue, editor.vue and the locale files are untouched; no new preference, panel, indicator or notification surface for endpoint or delivery state — the log is the surface for this change.

No server-start retry: a start_live_server failure (bind) keeps BLOCK_START_FAILED as a one-shot with its current meaning; only the endpoint file publication gains the bounded retry. No application-level restart, no scheduled or on-demand republication beyond the bounded attempt window, no change to cleanup_endpoint or the stale-PID logic.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first honest open: with the test-only emit-failure injection seam in the m045_ext emit path (cfg(test)-gated, invisible in release builds; the LiveServerState literal in main.rs stays textually unchanged), a fresh doc_open whose emission fails answers a non-2xx refusal with a plain {"error": ...} body and never accepted:true; no session survives (a patch echoing the refused session id and epoch is refused), a same-session resync whose emission fails restores the pre-resync session, the consumed epoch is never reused (a later successful open carries a strictly higher epoch), and the refusal is logged as a distinct state. Today the same interleaving logs and answers 200 accepted:true (live_server.rs:1540-1563), so every leg is red before the fix.

Success-path pin: an emission that succeeds keeps the exact response and event contract — 200 {accepted: true, revision: 1} and one doc_open event with the ordered identity fields — pinned alongside the refusal so the fix cannot over-reach; the existing stream identity/ownership and budget suites keep passing unchanged.

Failing-first endpoint publication: with the injected writer, a publication that fails transiently succeeds within the bounded attempt budget with each retry logged distinctly, and a first-attempt success writes exactly once as today; a permanent failure exhausts exactly the named attempt count and ends in the distinct "running but unpublished" final state whose marker is textually distinct from BLOCK_START_FAILED. Today there is a single write attempt and one log line (main.rs:838-843), so every leg is red before the fix.

Failing-first body bounds: an extension answering non-2xx with a multi-kilobyte body full of control characters yields an InvokeError.message within the named bound, free of raw control characters, carrying the explicit truncation marker with the original size — today the body is embedded verbatim and unbounded (invoke.rs:219-227), so the pin is red before the fix. The 503/429 retry path, the loopback and redirect pins keep passing unchanged (#321 suites), and a success path error message (parse failure, client-build failure) stays bounded under the same constant.

Failing-first renderer mapping: mt_ext_invoke against a scripted non-2xx extension returns an error string that names the failure class and status and states the body was withheld, containing no fragment of the extension body — today format!("{e}") returns the raw, body-bearing Display text (mod.rs:296-301), so the pin is red before the fix. The journal line keeps the bounded, sanitized, marker-carrying excerpt via Display, so the log loses no bounded diagnostic value while the renderer loses the foreign material entirely.

All predecessor suites named in Constraints pass with unchanged assertions after the fix (zero moved pins); the m045_ext cargo suite and the live-store/liveViewer vitest suites are green; graph ownership, module maps and file-local contracts (M-045: main.rs setup block, live_server.rs, live_bridge.rs, live_endpoint.rs, invoke.rs, mod.rs) describe the final implementation, with module contracts carrying the honest-refusal, bounded-retry and sanitization documentation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The named failing-first behaviors — the honest open refusal (non-2xx, no surviving session, resync restored, epoch never reused, distinct logged state), the endpoint publication retry (transient success within the budget, exhaustion distinct from the start failure, first-attempt success unchanged), the invoke body bounds with the truncation marker, and the body-free renderer mapping — each fail before the fix and pass after it. The C-STREAM-BUDGET, stream-security, #321 invoke and #326 trust suites pass unchanged in meaning (zero moved pins); the live-store and liveViewer vitest suites stay green, proving the preserved C-SEC-STREAM-TABS frontend contract. No renderer file is in the write scope, so no renderer-change suite is required. Before archiving: grace lint --path . --change C-EXT-DELIVERY-HONESTY --assertions final --run-commands, then grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json.

Assumptions.Assumption: The emit-failure refusal status is a 500-class internal refusal (the pairing-state-unavailable and context-channel-closed precedents in the same file); the exact status constant, error reason wording and log-marker names are plan-level constants within the bounds pinned here (non-2xx, plain {"error": ...} body, distinct logged state, session rollback under the already-held stream_gate and session lock — in-memory work only, no lock-order change).

The emit-failure injection seam is a test-only, cfg(test)-gated mechanism inside m045_ext (live_bridge.rs or live_server.rs), invisible in release builds; a seam that would require changing the LiveServerState literal in main.rs is rejected (the #321/#326 read-only-literal discipline). The endpoint retry helper takes the writer as an injection point for deterministic tests; main.rs calls the real writer.

The endpoint publication retry targets only the endpoint file write; a failure that survives the bounded attempt window is accepted for the process lifetime and surfaced as the distinct "running but unpublished" state — a missing live-endpoint.json stays an honest missing file for external consumers, and no publication-later mechanism (watcher, on-demand rewrite, restart) is planned.

The invoke message bound applies to every InvokeError.message and is of the order of a few hundred characters; sanitization neutralizes control characters and truncates with an explicit original-size marker — it does not attempt content-level redaction or secret scanning. The renderer mapping withholds the BadStatus body entirely; messages of non-body error kinds (capability-not-found, URL refusal, client-build failure) may keep their existing text under the same bound, since no extension-controlled body is involved.

AffectedAreas stays M-045-only, following the C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND and C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE precedent: the renderer files this change deliberately preserves are M-011-owned and untouched by design; main.rs is touched only inside its in-source M-045-annotated setup block (main.rs:817-852), and the graph files in the write scope exist solely to keep M-045's synchronized surface honest at implementation time.

Approval of this draft specification approves neither an unwritten plan nor apply/archive, lane departure or release; the seam mechanism, the refusal status and reason strings, the log-marker names, the attempt/pause and message-bound constants are plan-level within the bounds pinned here.
